C-STABILIZE-SPLIT-READING.Summary: Split View synchronizes content (150 ms debounce, C-29) but never scrolling: when split turns on, the second pane opens at the document top while the rich pane keeps a numeric scrollTop through the re-wrap — so the reading position "flies away somewhere" (owner quote 2026-10-27) — and scrolling either pane never moves the other (probe 2026-10-27: rich pane scrollTop 10339 of 11071, source pane 0 of 10856, same document). This change ships three behaviors: (1) typewriter-style anchor stability — every split layout transition (toggle on, toggle off, divider drag, width re-activation) centers the caret block — or, without a caret, the top visible block — in the pane instead of preserving a meaningless numeric offset; (2) initial alignment — the second pane opens at the editable pane's scroll fraction, never at the top by accident; (3) live bidirectional proportional scroll sync with an input-driven master and a re-entrancy guard, so reading either pane keeps the other in the same region of the document.

Goals.R-1: Anchor stability on split transitions: when split turns on (or the container crosses the 800px activation width), the editable pane keeps the reading anchor instead of a numeric scrollTop. The anchor is the caret block when the tab has one (live caret, or the saved cursor from C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY), otherwise the top visible block; the pane centers that anchor vertically (typewriter-style, the existing scrollToCursor/cursorCoords mechanics, target = pane middle), clamped at document edges. Toggle-off applies the same re-anchoring to the remaining single pane. Divider drags keep the anchor visible under the same rule.
Goals.R-2: Initial alignment of the second pane: when it mounts — split toggled on, tab switched while split is on, split re-activated after a width collapse — it opens aligned to the editable pane's current scroll fraction (scrollTop = fraction x scrollHeight, clamped), never at the document top by accident.
Goals.R-3: Live scroll sync: while split is active, scrolling either pane scrolls the other proportionally. The pane the user scrolls (wheel, touch, scrollbar, keyboard scroll) is the master and drives the other; programmatic sync echoes are dropped by a re-entrancy guard so the two panes never fight. Scroll movements that the editing surface itself produces (caret scroll-into-view, animatedScrollTo) sync like any other scroll, so the second pane follows where the edit landed. Sync stops cleanly on toggle-off, tab switch and unmount — no leaked listeners, no stale timers.
Goals.R-4: A sync controller owns anchor computation, fraction mapping, clamping and the re-entrancy guard, with pure unit-testable helpers (placement — a new util module vs splitView.vue-local, and the module/V-M anchors, new or M-011/V-M-011 extensions — are fixed by the plan after grace lint --parallel-preflight against the active changes in the tree). MODULE_CONTRACT / MODULE_MAP / CHANGE_SUMMARY update in every touched file; graph and verification route in the same bundle as the code.

AcceptanceCriteria.Criterion: Toggle-on anchoring: a long document scrolled to its middle with a caret placed mid-document, on split enable, shows the caret's block vertically centered in the rich pane and the source pane aligned to the same reading fraction (offsets within the pane height; scrollTop 0 only when the anchor itself is the document top); the no-caret variant anchors on the top visible block. Toggle-off re-anchors the remaining pane the same way.
Initial alignment: tab switch while split is on, and split re-activation after a width collapse, both land the second pane at the editable pane's fraction, not the top.

Live sync: scrolling the rich pane moves the source pane proportionally and vice versa, for wheel and scrollbar input; a programmatic echo does not re-trigger sync (no feedback loop observable across alternating scrolls); sync stops on toggle-off and tab switch with no stale listeners.

Governance: sync controller helpers unit-tested (fraction mapping, clamping, guard state machine); e2e suites above added; MODULE_CONTRACT/MAP/CHANGE_SUMMARY updated in touched files; graph and verification deltas routed with content-free markers; grace lint shows no new errors beyond the recorded pre-existing baseline.

NonGoals.NonGoal: Anything about pane editability (C-SPLIT-DUAL-EDIT owns it) or the dblclick toggle affordance (C-SPLIT-DBLCLICK-TOGGLE owns it).
Line-exact block-to-source anchor mapping: sync is proportional v1; the drift on height-skewed documents (code fences vs paragraphs) is accepted and recorded.
Cross-pane caret/selection mirroring or highlight sync.
Split below the 800px container collapse, split in Diff Mode, mobile/tablet split surfaces.
Changing the split keyboard shortcut, the menu item, the ratio persistence model, or the activation threshold.

C-STABILIZE-SPLIT-READING.IntegrationConstraint: Transplant product hunks only, retaining current page-width, progressive-mount, export and renderer behavior. Root applies all routed projections centrally; this worker changes no versions, release artifacts, commits or pushed refs.

Constraints.Item: No muya core changes: anchoring uses the exposed surface (getSelection().cursorCoords, container scrolling) the way scrollToCursor already does; CodeMirror uses its public scroll API. The work lives in the editorWithTabs layer and one new util at most.

Existing gates stay green and unweakened: npm test, renderer suites, e2e. This change rewrites no existing contracts — the C-29 corners (per-tab state, ratio persistence, narrow collapse, swap, `* item` normalization, mirror read-only) keep passing; new suites are added alongside.

Performance honesty on huge documents: sync reads are rAF-throttled and off the per-scroll-event hot path (no synchronous layout thrash); the adaptive mirror re-render debounce (2x last render time, cap 2 s) is unchanged.

The working tree carries parallel active changes (C-FILE-POSITION-MEMORY wiring, theme work); the plan runs grace lint --parallel-preflight before any write and reconciles observed-write overlaps instead of assuming them.
No new user-facing strings. No release or train admission follows from approval; version bumps and tags stay behind their separate owner instruction. English only in all committed artifacts.

AffectedAreas.Item: src/renderer/src/components/editorWithTabs/ — splitView.vue (controller wiring), editor.vue (anchor re-centering, sync hooks), sourceCode.vue (initial alignment, live sync), index.vue (wiring only if the controller placement requires it).
New sync controller (util module or splitView-local, fixed by the plan) with pure helpers.
tests/ — new e2e suites for anchoring and sync; new renderer unit suites for the controller helpers.
.grace/graph/* and .grace/verification/* — routing deltas for the touched modules and scenarios, in the same bundle as the code.
Explicitly out of write scope: src-tauri, src/muya internals, static/locales, CI workflows.
